title: Jupiter's Storm Plunges 200 Miles Deep
description: Jupiter's iconic Great Red Spot isn't just a surface cloud feature. NASA's Juno mission revealed the storm plunges hundreds of miles into the planet's deep atmosphere.

beats.text: Jupiter's famous storm plunges 200 miles deep into its atmosphere.
beats.visual: Jupiter's Great Red Spot as seen by NASA's Juno spacecraft, 2019

beats.text: Most people assume it's just a thin surface cloud.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of Jupiter's cloud bands, 2019

beats.text: NASA's Juno spacecraft measured the planet's gravity to look inside.
beats.visual: Illustration of NASA's Juno spacecraft orbiting Jupiter, 2019

beats.text: It revealed a vertical vortex reaching far below the cloud tops.
beats.visual: Scientific visualization of the Great Red Spot's depth and structure, 2019

beats.text: These storm roots stretch past where solar light can reach.
beats.visual: Internal view of Jupiter's atmosphere showing light penetration levels, 2019

beats.text: Since Jupiter lacks a solid surface, there's no friction to stop it.
beats.visual: Wide shot of Jupiter's swirling storms and zones, Juno, 2019

beats.text: That lack of surface friction is why the storm plunges 200 miles deep.
beats.visual: Portrait of the Great Red Spot spinning on Jupiter's disk, 2019
